sentences.text: Messelirrisor were tiny birds that resembled modern hoopoes but were smaller in size.
Found specimens include complete and articulated skeletons along with preserved feather remains.
In the species M. parvus, beak length varies between individual specimens.
Fossils of Messelirrisor have been discovered at the Messel Pit in Hesse, Germany.
Messelirrisor is considered to be an arboreal bird.
Messelirrisor occupied the ecological niche of certain passerine groups before those birds had arrived in Europe.
Messelirrisor may have been insectivorous, as its beak shape is similar to that of other hoopoe and wood-hoopoe groups.
Messelirrisor is the only genus in the extinct family Messelirrisoridae within the order Bucerotiformes.
The family Messelirrisoridae represents the oldest known group including modern hoopoes (Upupidae) and wood-hoopoes (Phoeniculidae).
These birds were common small forest inhabitants of Central Europe during the Middle Eocene, approximately 49 to 37 million years ago.
Messelirrisor lived in forests covering Central Europe during the Middle Eocene, between 53 and 49 million years ago.
The time range for Messelirrisor is the Lutetian stage, from 48.07 to 41.03 million years ago.
